### Introduccion
1. Correlation Analysis
The goal of this step is to identify CpG sites whose methylation levels correlate with the inferred cell type proportions.

Steps:
Prepare the data:
- Ensure your EPIC array methylation data (e.g., beta-values or M-values) and CIBERSORTx cell type proportions are in the same sample order.
- Use a matrix where rows represent CpGs and columns represent samples for methylation data, and a matrix where rows represent cell types and columns represent samples for cell type proportions.

Choose a correlation method:
- Use Pearson correlation if the data is normally distributed.
- Use Spearman correlation if the data is not normally distributed or if you suspect non-linear relationships.

Perform correlation for each CpG-cell type pair:
- Loop through each CpG site and calculate its correlation with each cell type proportion.

Adjust for multiple testing:
- Since you are testing thousands of CpGs, apply a multiple testing correction like False Discovery Rate (FDR) or Bonferroni.

# Cell portions with statistical evaluation between conditions
- Test for statistically significant differences between groups. I use wilcoxon rank sum test, since the proportion distributions are not normal, cell proportions are bound between 0 and 1. The variance als is not constant.

- Sample sizes per group may be small (<30)
- t-tests assume normality, which is hard to verify with small samples
- Wilcoxon is more robust with limited data


```{r}
# Your data preparation code
cols <- c("SEO_COPD_Y_or_N", CELL_TYPES_STATS)
df <- df.pheno.SEO.ES[, cols]
colnames(df) <- sub("^MuSiC_", "", colnames(df))   # drop the source prefix from all plot labels
colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "Alveolar.macrophages"] <- "Alv.macrophages"

# Convert df to long format
df_long <- gather(
  df,
  key = "celltypes",
  value = "props",

# Save the plot

ggsave(
  filename = filename,
  plot = plt.prop.dist,
  device = "png",
  dpi = 300,
  width = 10,
  height = 8
)
```

```{r}
# Set your desired FDR threshold
fdr_threshold <- 0.05  

# Perform statistical tests for each cell type with custom FDR threshold
stat_test <- df_long %>%
  group_by(celltypes) %>%
  # Apply logit transformation with small constant to avoid infinite values
  mutate(
    # Add small constant to avoid 0 and 1, then apply logit transform
    logit_props = log((props + 0.001) / (1 - props + 0.001))
  ) %>%
  # Perform t-test on logit-transformed proportions
  rstatix::t_test(logit_props ~ SEO_COPD_Y_or_N) %>%
  adjust_pvalue(method = "fdr") %>%
  # Create custom significance labels based on your FDR threshold
  mutate(
    p.adj.signif = case_when(
      p.adj <= fdr_threshold & p.adj > 0.001 ~ paste0("FDR ≤ ", fdr_threshold),
      p.adj <= 0.001 ~ "***",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    )
  ) %>%
  add_xy_position(x = "celltypes", dodge = 0.8)

head(stat_test)
```

## Subset methylation mtx

```{r}
rownames(df.pheno.SEO.ES) <- df.pheno.SEO.ES$Row.names
# Subset samples
beta.values <- ENmix::M2B(win.m.values)
sample_keep =  which(rownames(df.pheno.SEO.ES) %in% base::colnames(beta.values))
pheno.data = df.pheno.SEO.ES[sample_keep,]
rownames(pheno.data) <- pheno.data$Row.names

idx.subjects <- match(pheno.data$Row.names, base::colnames(beta.values))
mtx.beta.values <- as.matrix(beta.values[,idx.subjects])
dim(mtx.beta.values)

mtx.m.values <- as.matrix(win.m.values[,idx.subjects])
dim(mtx.m.values)
```

```{r}
cpg.ids <- SEO.sig.DMPs$CpG.id

# Pre-extract methylation data for all CpGs at once
m.values <- mtx.m.values[cpg.ids, rownames(pheno.data), drop = FALSE]
beta.values<- mtx.beta.values[cpg.ids, rownames(pheno.data), drop = FALSE]

#"SEO_COPD_Y_or_N"
cell.type.proportions <- pheno.data[, c("Row.names", CELL_TYPES_CORR)]

cell.type.proportions <- as.data.frame(cell.type.proportions)
rownames(cell.type.proportions) <- cell.type.proportions$Row.names
cell.type.proportions <- cell.type.proportions[, -1]
# drop the source prefix: cell-type names feed every plot, heatmap and results table below
colnames(cell.type.proportions) <- sub("^MuSiC_", "", colnames(cell.type.proportions))

# Initialize results list
results <- list()

# Loop through each cell type
for (cell.type in colnames(cell.type.proportions)) {
  # Extract proportions for this cell type
  proportions <- as.numeric(cell.type.proportions[, cell.type])
  
  # Calculate correlations and p-values in one pass for efficiency
  corr.results <- apply(
    beta.values,
    1,
    function(cpg) {
      # Handle missing values
      complete.cases <- complete.cases(cpg, proportions)
      cpg.clean <- cpg[complete.cases]
      prop.clean <- proportions[complete.cases]
      
      # Skip if not enough observations
      if (length(cpg.clean) < 3) {
        return(list(correlation = NA, p.value = NA))
      }
      
      # Calculate correlation with exact=FALSE to handle ties
      ct <- suppressWarnings(
        cor.test(cpg.clean, prop.clean, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
      )
      # Return correlation and p-value
      list(correlation = ct$estimate, p.value = ct$p.value)
    }
  )
  
  # Extract results
  correlations <- sapply(corr.results, function(x) x$correlation)
  p.values <- sapply(corr.results, function(x) x$p.value)

 
  # Handle NA values before p-value adjustment
  na.mask <- !is.na(p.values)
  adj.p.values <- rep(NA, length(p.values))
  adj.p.values[na.mask] <- p.adjust(p.values[na.mask], method = "fdr")
  
  # Store results in a data frame
  results[[cell.type]] <- data.frame(
    CpG = rownames(beta.values),
    Correlation = correlations,
    P.Value = p.values,
    Adj.P.Value = adj.p.values,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Remove temporary variables
  rm(corr.results, correlations, p.values, adj.p.values)
}

results
```

```{r}
plot_specific_cpgs <- function(results, beta.values, cell.type.proportions, cpgs, output_dir = NULL) {
  # Check if all requested CpGs are available
  missing_cpgs <- base::setdiff(cpgs, rownames(beta.values))
  if (length(missing_cpgs) > 0) {
    warning(paste("The following CpGs were not found:", paste(missing_cpgs, collapse = ", ")))
    cpgs <- intersect(cpgs, rownames(beta.values))
  }
  
  if (length(cpgs) == 0) {
    stop("No valid CpGs provided")
  }
  
  # Loop through each cell type
  for (cell.type in colnames(cell.type.proportions)) {
    # Prepare data for plotting
    plot_data <- as.data.frame(t(beta.values[cpgs, , drop = FALSE]))
    plot_data$Sample <- rownames(plot_data)
    
    plot_data <- merge(
      plot_data,
      data.frame(
        Sample = rownames(cell.type.proportions),
        logit_proportion = log((cell.type.proportions[, cell.type] + 1e-6) / (1 - cell.type.proportions[, cell.type] + 1e-6))
      ),
      by = "Sample"
    )

    # Convert to long format for ggplot
    plot_data_long <- melt(plot_data, 
                           id.vars = c("Sample", "logit_proportion"),
                           variable.name = "CpG", 
                           value.name = "Methylation")
    
    # Add correlation information to the plot
    res_cell <- results[[cell.type]]
    annotation_df <- data.frame(
      CpG = cpgs,
      Correlation = res_cell$Correlation[match(cpgs, res_cell$CpG)],
      P.Value = res_cell$P.Value[match(cpgs, res_cell$CpG)]
    )
    annotation_df$Label <- paste0("r = ", round(annotation_df$Correlation, 3), 
                                 "\np = ", signif(annotation_df$P.Value, 3))
    
    # Create plot
    p <- ggplot(plot_data_long, aes(x = logit_proportion, y = Methylation)) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
      geom_text(data = annotation_df, 
                aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = Label), 
                hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.1, size = 3) +
      facet_wrap(~ CpG, scales = "free_y") +
      labs(title = paste("Specific CpGs vs", cell.type, "logit_proportion"),
           x = paste(cell.type, "logit_proportion"),
           y = "Methylation (Beta)") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
    
    # Save or display plot
    if (!is.null(output_dir)) {
      if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
        dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
      }
      ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0("SpecificCpGs_", cell.type, "_logit_prop.png")), 
             p, width = 7, height = 5)
    } else {
      print(p)
    }
  }
}
```


```{r}
plot_specific_cpgs <- function(results, beta.values, cell.type.proportions, cpgs, output_dir = NULL) {
  # Check if all requested CpGs are available
  missing_cpgs <- base::setdiff(cpgs, rownames(beta.values))
  if (length(missing_cpgs) > 0) {
    warning(paste("The following CpGs were not found:", paste(missing_cpgs, collapse = ", ")))
    cpgs <- intersect(cpgs, rownames(beta.values))
  }
  
  if (length(cpgs) == 0) {
    stop("No valid CpGs provided")
  }
  
  # Loop through each cell type
  for (cell.type in colnames(cell.type.proportions)) {
    # Prepare data for plotting
    plot_data <- as.data.frame(t(beta.values[cpgs, , drop = FALSE]))
    plot_data$Sample <- rownames(plot_data)
    
    plot_data <- merge(
      plot_data,
      data.frame(
        Sample = rownames(cell.type.proportions),
        proportion = cell.type.proportions[, cell.type],
        log2_proportion = log2(cell.type.proportions[, cell.type] + 1e-6), # add small constant to avoid log(0)
        logit_proportion = log(
                            cell.type.proportions[,cell.type] + 1e-6
                            ) / (1 - cell.type.proportions[,cell.type] + 1e-6) 
        ),
      by = "Sample"
    )

    # Convert to long format for ggplot
    plot_data_long <- melt(plot_data, 
                           #id.vars = c("Sample", "proportion"), 
                           id.vars = c(
                             "Sample",
                             #"log2_proportion",
                             "logit_proportion"
                             ),
                           variable.name = "CpG", 
                           value.name = "Methylation")
    
    # Add correlation information to the plot
    res_cell <- results[[cell.type]]
    annotation_df <- data.frame(
      CpG = cpgs,
      Correlation = res_cell$Correlation[match(cpgs, res_cell$CpG)],
      P.Value = res_cell$P.Value[match(cpgs, res_cell$CpG)]
    )
    annotation_df$Label <- paste0("r = ", round(annotation_df$Correlation, 3), 
                                 "\np = ", signif(annotation_df$P.Value, 3))
    
    # Create plot
    p <- ggplot(plot_data_long, aes(x = logit_proportion, y = Methylation)) +
      #geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
       geom_point(
        fill = "#377EB8", 
        size = 3, 
        alpha = 0.8,
        shape = 21,
        color = "black",
        stroke = 1
      ) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "blue") +
      geom_text(data = annotation_df, 
                aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = Label), 
                hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.1, size = 3) +
      facet_wrap(~ CpG, scales = "free_y") +
      labs(title = paste("Specific CpGs vs", cell.type, "logit_proportion"),
           x = paste(cell.type, "logit_proportion"),
           y = "Methylation (Beta)") +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 16),
        axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8),
        axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines")
      )
    
    #  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
    
    # Save or display plot
    if (!is.null(output_dir)) {
      if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
        dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
      }
      ggsave(file.path(output_dir, paste0("SpecificCpGs_", cell.type, "_logit_prop.png")), 
             p, width = 10, height = 5)
    } else {
      print(p)
    }
  }
}
```

# Visualization of correlation results

```{r}
results.dir.plots.corr <- file.path(paste0(results.dir.plots, "corr_heatmaps/"))
dir.create(results.dir.plots.corr, recursive = TRUE)

corr.mtx <- sapply(results, function(x) x$Correlation)
rownames(corr.mtx) <- results[[1]]$CpG  # Assuming CpG order is consistent
sig.cor.matrix <- sapply(results, function(x) ifelse(x$Adj.P.Value < 0.05, "*", ""))
rownames(sig.cor.matrix) <- rownames(corr.mtx)


pheatmap(
  mat = corr.mtx,
  display_numbers = sig.cor.matrix[rownames(corr.mtx), ],
  color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),  # Diverging color scale
  breaks = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 100),                     # Scale from -1 to 1
  cluster_rows = FALSE,                                      # Cluster CpGs
  cluster_cols = FALSE,                                      # Cluster cell types
  show_rownames = FALSE,                                     # Hide CpG names (too many)
  show_colnames = TRUE,                                      # Show cell type names
  main = "Correlation Heatmap: CpGs vs. Cell Types",
  fontsize_col = 12,                                           # Adjust column font
  na_col = "grey",
  filename = file.path(results.dir.plots.corr, "corr_heatmap_all_cpgs_fdr_005.png"),
)
```

# Correlation heatmap of significant cpgs vs cell types

```{r}
# Filter for significant CpGs (Adj.P.Value < 0.05)
sig.cpgs <- Reduce(base::union, lapply(results, function(x) x$CpG[x$Adj.P.Value < 0.05]))
cor.matrix.filtered <- corr.mtx[rownames(corr.mtx) %in% sig.cpgs, ]

pval.mtx <- sapply(results, function(x) x$Adj.P.Value)
rownames(pval.mtx) <- results[[1]]$CpG  # Assuming CpG order is consistent

pval.mtx.filtered <- pval.mtx[rownames(pval.mtx) %in% sig.cpgs, ]

# 2. Create labels matrix using the filtered matrices
labels.matrix <- matrix( 
  NA_character_, 
  nrow = nrow(cor.matrix.filtered),
  ncol = ncol(cor.matrix.filtered),
  dimnames = dimnames(cor.matrix.filtered)
)

# 3. Fill the labels matrix safely
for (i in 1:nrow(cor.matrix.filtered)) {
  for (j in 1:ncol(cor.matrix.filtered)) {
    if (!is.na(cor.matrix.filtered[i,j])) {
      labels.matrix[i,j] <- sprintf(
        "%.2f%s", 
        cor.matrix.filtered[i,j], 
        ifelse(pval.mtx.filtered[i,j] < 0.1, "*", "")
      )
    } else {
      labels.matrix[i,j] <- ""
    }
  }
}

# Replace NA correlations (e.g., due to insufficient data) with empty strings
labels.matrix[is.na(cor.matrix.filtered)] <- ""

pheatmap(
  mat = cor.matrix.filtered,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),  # Diverging color scale
  breaks = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 100),                     # Scale from -1 to 1
  cluster_rows = TRUE,                                        # Cluster CpGs
  cluster_cols = FALSE,                                        # Cluster cell types
  show_rownames = TRUE,                                      # Hide CpG names (too many)
  show_colnames = TRUE,
  number_color = "black",
  display_numbers = labels.matrix, # Show cell type names
  main = "Correlation Heatmap: CpGs vs. Cell Types",
  fontsize_col = 12,                                           # Adjust column font
  na_col = "grey",
  angle_row = 45,
  height = 7,         # Control overall dimensions
  width = 5,
  filename = file.path(results.dir.plots.corr, "corr_heatmap_sig_cpgs_celltype_fdr005.png"),
)
```

```{r}
# Filter for significant CpGs (Adj.P.Value < 0.05)
sig.cpgs <- Reduce(base::union, lapply(results, function(x) x$CpG[x$Adj.P.Value < 0.05]))
cor.matrix.filtered <- corr.mtx[rownames(corr.mtx) %in% sig.cpgs, ]

pval.mtx <- sapply(results, function(x) x$Adj.P.Value)
rownames(pval.mtx) <- results[[1]]$CpG  # Assuming CpG order is consistent

pval.mtx.filtered <- pval.mtx[rownames(pval.mtx) %in% sig.cpgs, ]

# TRANSPOSE the matrices to get CpGs in columns and cell types in rows
cor.matrix.filtered.t <- t(cor.matrix.filtered)
pval.mtx.filtered.t <- t(pval.mtx.filtered)

# 2. Create labels matrix using the TRANSPOSED filtered matrices
labels.matrix <- matrix( 
  NA_character_, 
  nrow = nrow(cor.matrix.filtered.t),
  ncol = ncol(cor.matrix.filtered.t),
  dimnames = dimnames(cor.matrix.filtered.t)
)

# 3. Fill the labels matrix safely
for (i in 1:nrow(cor.matrix.filtered.t)) {
  for (j in 1:ncol(cor.matrix.filtered.t)) {
    if (!is.na(cor.matrix.filtered.t[i,j])) {
      labels.matrix[i,j] <- sprintf(
        "%.2f%s", 
        cor.matrix.filtered.t[i,j], 
        ifelse(pval.mtx.filtered.t[i,j] < 0.1, "*", "")
      )
    } else {
      labels.matrix[i,j] <- ""
    }
  }
}

# Replace NA correlations (e.g., due to insufficient data) with empty strings
labels.matrix[is.na(cor.matrix.filtered.t)] <- ""

pheatmap(
  mat = cor.matrix.filtered.t,  # Use transposed matrix
  color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),  # Diverging color scale
  breaks = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 100),                     # Scale from -1 to 1
  cluster_rows = FALSE,                                       # Cluster cell types (now rows)
  cluster_cols = TRUE,                                        # Cluster CpGs (now columns)
  show_rownames = TRUE,                                      # Show cell type names (now rows)
  show_colnames = TRUE,                                      # Show CpG names (now columns)
  number_color = "black",
  display_numbers = labels.matrix, # Show correlation values with asterisks
  main = "Correlation Heatmap: Cell Types vs. CpGs",
  fontsize_col = 8,                                           # Smaller font for CpG names
  fontsize_row = 12,                                          # Larger font for cell types
  na_col = "grey",
  angle_col = 90,                                            # Rotate CpG names
  height = 5,                                                # Adjust dimensions
  width = 3,
  filename = file.path(results.dir.plots.corr, "corr_heatmap_cpg_vs_celltypes_fdr005.png"),
)
```

### 2. Linear Regression Modeling
For CpGs showing significant correlations with cell type proportions, you can refine the analysis by performing linear regression while adjusting for potential confounders (e.g., age, sex, smoking status).

Steps:
Prepare covariates:
- Create a data.frame containing covariates such as age, sex, smoking status, batch effects, or other technical variables.

Run linear regression for each significant CpG:
- Use the methylation beta-value as the dependent variable.
- Use the cell type proportion as the independent variable.
- Include covariates in the model.

Extract results:
- For each CpG-cell type pair, extract the regression coefficient (β), p-value, and adjusted p-value.
- Adjust for multiple testing:
- Correct p-values across all tests using FDR or Bonferroni correction.


```{r}

# Ensure sample order matches between datasets
covariates <- pheno.data[colnames(beta.values), ]

# Initialize results storage for linear regression
regression.results <- list()

# Loop through each significant CpG and each cell type proportion
for (cpg in rownames(beta.values)) {
  for (cell.type in colnames(cell.type.proportions)) {
    # Create a data frame for modeling
    model.data <- data.frame(
      Methylation = beta.values[cpg, ],
      ct.proportion = as.numeric(cell.type.proportions[ , cell.type]),
      covariates
    )
    
    # Fit linear regression model
    model <- lm(Methylation ~ ct.proportion + SEO_COPD_Y_or_N + Age + Gender + PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + PC6 + PC7,
                data = model.data)
    
    # Extract coefficients and p-value for the cell type proportion term
    coef_summary <- summary(model)$coefficients["ct.proportion", ]
    
    # Store results
    regression.results[[paste(cpg, cell.type, sep = "_")]] <- data.frame(
      CpG = cpg,
      Cell_Type = cell.type,
      Beta = coef_summary["Estimate"],
      P.Value = coef_summary["Pr(>|t|)"]
    )
  }
}

# Combine all regression results into a single table
df.regr.results <- bind_rows(regression.results)

# Adjust p-values using FDR correction
df.regr.results$Adj.P.Value <- p.adjust(df.regr.results$P.Value, method = "fdr")

# Filter significant associations (e.g., FDR < 0.05)
filtered.sig.regr.results <- df.regr.results %>%
                        filter((P.Value < 0.05) & (Beta > 0.1 | Beta < -0.1))  # use nominal
                        
# Save results to file
write.csv(
  filtered.sig.regr.results,
  file.path("filtered_regression_cpgs_cell_types.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```


```{r}
df <- data.frame(
  CpG = filtered.sig.regr.results$CpG,
  Cell.Type = filtered.sig.regr.results$Cell_Type,
  Beta = filtered.sig.regr.results$Beta,
  P.Value = filtered.sig.regr.results$P.Value
)

# Create beta matrix (corrected)
beta.matrix <- df %>%
  dplyr::select(CpG, Cell.Type, Beta) %>%  # Note: Using Beta, not P.Value
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Cell.Type, 
    values_from = Beta
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("CpG") %>%
  as.matrix()

pval.matrix <- df %>%
  dplyr::select(CpG, Cell.Type, P.Value) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Cell.Type, 
    values_from = P.Value
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("CpG") %>%
  as.matrix()


# Create labels: Beta values + stars for significance
labels.matrix <- matrix(
  sprintf(
    "%.2g%s", 
    beta.matrix, 
    ifelse(pval.matrix < 0.05, "*", "")
  ),
  nrow = nrow(beta.matrix),
  dimnames = dimnames(beta.matrix)
)

#colOrder <- c("Smooth.muscle", "Dendritic.cells", "B.cell.lineage", "EC.venous", "Fibroblast.lineage", "Monocytes" , "EC.arterial", "AT2", "Alveolar.macrophages")
#beta.matrix <- beta.matrix[, colOrder]

pheatmap(

  number_color = "black",
  fontsize_number = 5,
  fontsize_row = 5,
  show_rownames = TRUE,            # Show CpG names on left
  show_colnames = TRUE,            # Show cell types on top
  cluster_rows = FALSE,            # Disable clustering (adjust as needed)
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
  breaks = seq(-max(abs(beta.matrix), na.rm = TRUE), 
               max(abs(beta.matrix), na.rm = TRUE), 
               length.out = 100),
  main = "DNA Methylation (Beta) by Cell Type",
  na_col = "grey"
)

```

### 3. Identify Significant Associations
After completing both correlation analysis and linear regression modeling:
- Focus on CpGs that show consistent significant associations across both analyses.
- Interpret these associations in the context of nearby genes and known biological functions   of the associated cell types.

Notes on Interpretation:
- A positive correlation or regression coefficient indicates that higher methylation at a CpG   is associated with higher abundance of a specific cell type.
- A negative correlation suggests that lower methylation is associated with higher abundance   of the cell type.
- Consider visualizing top hits using scatterplots to confirm patterns (e.g., ggplot2).
